svg.title: Risk of bias: the Core GRADE Guide Figure 7-2 decision as pmatools implements it
svg.desc: Flowchart. Is evidence dominated by high risk of bias studies? Possible thresholds for dominating are more than 65% of the weight, or 55% or more as possibly dominating; pmatools uses 55% by default. Yes: use results from all studies and rate down. No: appreciable evidence exists from low risk of bias studies, with corresponding thresholds of 35% or 45% of the weight, and the chart asks whether there are substantial differences in estimate of effect between high and low risk of bias studies. Yes: use only low risk of bias studies and do not rate down. No: use results from all studies and do not rate down. A comparison that cannot be made takes the No edge, and a body of evidence with no high risk of bias study takes that route too. This is pmatools’ operationalisation of the Core GRADE Guide Figure 7-2 decision (formerly Core GRADE 4 Figure 2), not a reproduction of the published figure: the Guide words the substantial-differences question qualitatively, and pmatools answers it with a change of zone relative to the chosen threshold or a relative change in magnitude of more than 20% in either direction. The legacy pmatools 0.5.x direction-of-bias check, which is beyond Core GRADE and available only on request, is not drawn.
svg.text: Risk of bias — Core GRADE Guide Fig 7-2, as pmatools implements it

text.tspan: Use results from all studies and rate down
Are there substantial differences in estimate of
effect between high and low risk of bias studies?
Use only low risk of bias
* Possible thresholds for high risk of bias ‘dominating’: >65% weight or ≥55% weight=possibly dominating (pmatools default: 55%).
† Possible thresholds for appreciable low risk of bias evidence, corresponding to thresholds for high risk of bias dominating, ≥35% or ≥45% weight.
After the Core GRADE Guide (Guyatt et al.) Figure 7-2, formerly Core GRADE 4 Figure 2. pmatools’ operationalisation, not a reproduction:
the numbers that answer the substantial-differences question are pmatools’; see ?grade_flowcharts.
